title.es: Construir sobre la idea de otro

es: Aportar una opinión concordando parcialmente, ampliar lo dicho por otro con un ejemplo y devolver el turno con una pregunta a otro participante.

vocabulary.es: entiendo lo que dices, tienes razón en eso
hasta cierto punto, en cierta medida

teaching.en: I agree up to a point, but I see one drawback: a ban would treat the symptom and ignore the cause.
teaching.es: Estoy de acuerdo hasta cierto punto, pero veo un inconveniente: una prohibición trataría el síntoma e ignoraría la causa.
teaching.explanationEs: Up to a point limita el acuerdo; después de but aparece el matiz (aquí, un drawback).
segments: I agree up to a point, but I see one drawback:
a ban would treat the symptom and ignore the cause.
teaching.audioText: I agree up to a point, but I see one drawback: a ban would treat the symptom and ignore the cause.

teaching.en: I take your point, and it is a valid point, although I partly disagree with the conclusion you draw from it.
teaching.es: Entiendo lo que dices, y es un punto válido, aunque discrepo en parte de la conclusión que sacas de él.
teaching.explanationEs: I take your point reconoce la idea del otro sin aceptar su conclusión; partly suaviza el desacuerdo.
segments: I take your point, and it is a valid point, although
I partly disagree with the conclusion you draw from it.
teaching.audioText: I take your point, and it is a valid point, although I partly disagree with the conclusion you draw from it.

teaching.en: Building on what my fellow participant said, I would go further and, for instance, give every school a clear rule.
teaching.es: Partiendo de lo que dijo mi compañero de mesa, yo iría más lejos y, por ejemplo, daría a cada colegio una norma clara.
teaching.explanationEs: Building on + lo dicho amplía; I would go further anuncia que llevas la idea más allá que el otro.
segments: Building on what my fellow participant said, I would go
further and, for instance, give every school a clear rule.
teaching.audioText: Building on what my fellow participant said, I would go further and, for instance, give every school a clear rule.

teaching.en: For instance, in my school, tablets saved hours of copying, yet few pupils read more as a result.
teaching.es: Por ejemplo, en mi colegio las tablets ahorraron horas de copia, pero pocos alumnos leyeron más como resultado.
teaching.explanationEs: For instance + coma introduce un caso concreto; yet añade un matiz que limita el ejemplo.
segments: For instance, in my school, tablets saved hours of
copying, yet few pupils read more as a result.
teaching.audioText: For instance, in my school, tablets saved hours of copying, yet few pupils read more as a result.

teaching.en: Furthermore, the idea works best when parents help, and I would like to flesh out that point briefly.
teaching.es: Además, la idea funciona mejor cuando los padres ayudan, y me gustaría desarrollar ese punto brevemente.
teaching.explanationEs: Furthermore suma un argumento; flesh out + punto anuncia que vas a desarrollarlo con más detalle.
segments: Furthermore, the idea works best when parents help, and
I would like to flesh out that point briefly.
teaching.audioText: Furthermore, the idea works best when parents help, and I would like to flesh out that point briefly.

teaching.en: To a certain extent the trial worked, but its main drawback was the extra time that teachers needed to prepare.
teaching.es: Hasta cierto punto la prueba funcionó, pero su principal inconveniente fue el tiempo extra que los profesores necesitaron para prepararse.
teaching.explanationEs: To a certain extent es sinónimo de up to a point; se usa igual para acotar un acuerdo o un éxito.
segments: To a certain extent the trial worked, but its main
drawback was the extra time that teachers needed to prepare.
teaching.audioText: To a certain extent the trial worked, but its main drawback was the extra time that teachers needed to prepare.

prompt.es: Completa: «Veo un inconveniente: castigaría a quienes usan el celular para aprender.»

feedback.es: Drawback es el inconveniente que matiza un acuerdo parcial; downside y disadvantage son sinónimos válidos.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo que nombra el punto débil de una idea.

origin.text: I accept that a complete ban would make things easier, but I see one ___: it would hurt the students who use phones to learn.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Entiendo tu punto, pero discrepo en parte.»

answer.text: I take your point, but I partly disagree

feedback.es: I take your point reconoce la idea y but partly disagree matiza el desacuerdo.

hint.es: Empieza con la fórmula que reconoce la idea del otro.

choices.text: I agree completely, Leo, and I can see no drawback at all in a ban.
I disagree entirely, Leo, because phones are useful in every class.
I agree up to a point, but I see one drawback for some learners.

feedback.es: Up to a point y un drawback dejan ver un acuerdo con reservas; las otras respuestas aceptan o rechazan del todo.

hint.es: El acuerdo parcial acepta algo y luego matiza.

origin.text: Leo: Schools should ban phones completely.

prompt.es: Completa: «Partiendo de su idea, añadiría que casi no cuestan nada.»

feedback.es: Building on + idea ajena es la fórmula para ampliar; expanding on funciona igual.

origin.text: Mia made a good case for more outdoor lessons. ___ on her idea, I would add that they cost almost nothing.

prompt.es: ¿Qué intervención amplía la idea de Mia en lugar de repetirla?

choices.text: Building on that, phones could stay in a box during lessons and come out at break.
I agree with Mia: screens distract children in class, and that is a serious problem for teachers.
Mia is wrong: screens distract children far less than noise does in most rooms.

feedback.es: Añade una propuesta nueva que parte de lo dicho; las otras repiten la idea o la rechazan.

origin.text: Mia: Screens distract children in class, especially when a message arrives in the middle of an explanation.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿cómo interviene la oradora en el debate?

choices.text: She accepts part of the idea, gives a benefit and then asks Tom to prove that it is real.
She accepts part of the idea, gives a benefit and then asks Tom what he has seen.
She accepts part of the idea, gives a benefit and then answers her own question about reading.

feedback.es: Acepta parte de la idea, aporta un beneficio (la hoja que nadie perdió) y termina preguntando a Tom qué ha observado.

origin.audio: I can see what you mean, and to a certain extent I agree. Tablets made our lessons tidier. For instance, nobody lost a worksheet all term. But did reading improve? Tom, you teach the older group: what did you notice?

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención: acuerdo parcial, ampliación con ejemplo y una pregunta.

answer.text: Thank you, Leo. I take your point, and I agree with you up to a point. Tablets are light, they are cheap to update, and a child can carry a whole library in one bag. But I see one drawback in a complete switch: many pupils read more slowly on a screen, and they get distracted by notifications. For instance, last month my teacher asked us to read a short story on a tablet, and half of the class ended up checking messages. Building on your idea, I would suggest a simple compromise: tablets for research and exercises, and paper for long reading. Furthermore, we could ask pupils to help us write the rules, because people follow what they choose. That is partly why I would not remove paper completely. Mia, what have you noticed with the younger children you work with? Do they read better on paper or on a screen? I would like to hear your view before we decide anything.
accepted: Thank you, Leo. I take your point, and I agree with you up to a point. Tablets are light, they are cheap to update, and a child can carry a whole library in one bag. But I see one drawback in a complete switch: many pupils read more slowly on a screen, and they get distracted by notifications. For instance, last month my teacher asked us to read a short story on a tablet, and half of the class ended up checking messages. Building on your idea, I would suggest a simple compromise: tablets for research and exercises, and paper for long reading. Furthermore, we could ask pupils to help us write the rules, because people follow what they choose. That is partly why I would not remove paper completely. Mia, what have you noticed with the younger children you work with? Do they read better on paper or on a screen? I would like to hear your view before we decide anything.

Thanks, Leo. That is a fair point, and to a certain extent I agree with you, because tablets really do save a lot of weight and money. However, I see one problem: a screen makes it easy to open something else. For example, yesterday I tried to read a chapter on my tablet and I answered four messages before the end of the first page. Expanding on your idea, I would like to propose that every school keeps a set of paper books for long reading, and uses tablets for everything else. I would add that pupils should choose the books themselves, because a child reads more when the book belongs to them. Mia, what is your experience with the youngest pupils? Would the same plan work for them, or do they need something different? I am curious about your view, and I would like to hear it before we make any decision.

feedback.es: Una buena intervención reconoce lo válido, matiza el acuerdo, amplía con un ejemplo y devuelve el turno con una pregunta a Mia.

origin.text: Mesa redonda sobre libros y tablets. Leo dijo: «Los colegios deberían sustituir los libros de papel por tablets». Responde en inglés (150–230 palabras): reconoce lo válido de su idea, expresa un acuerdo parcial (up to a point, partly), amplía con un ejemplo (for instance) y termina con una pregunta dirigida a otra participante, Mia.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué hace la oradora con la idea de Leo?

choices.text: She accepts the whole idea and adds an example to support it.
She accepts part of the idea and then asks Leo for evidence.
She accepts part of the idea but adds a problem.

feedback.es: «Up to a point» limita su acuerdo con Leo, y el «But» introduce el problema: el estrés de algunos alumnos.

origin.audio: Homework builds habits, and I agree with Leo up to a point. But for some pupils it only adds stress, and I have seen that with my own eyes. Take the case of my neighbour's son: he finishes his homework at ten at night and then cannot sleep. Furthermore, the teachers who set the most homework rarely have time to mark it properly, so the effort often disappears without a word of feedback. So I would not remove homework completely; I would reduce it, and I would make sure that every task counts for something.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué da a entender sobre los profesores que mandan más tareas?

choices.text: That they may not give it the attention it deserves.
That they do not believe that it builds good habits.
That they are unaware of the stress that it causes.

feedback.es: Dice que rara vez tienen tiempo de corregirlos bien: sugiere que las tareas reciben menos atención de la debida.

origin.audio: Homework builds habits, and I agree with Leo up to a point. But for some pupils it only adds stress, and I have seen that with my own eyes. Take the case of my neighbour's son: he finishes his homework at ten at night and then cannot sleep. Furthermore, the teachers who set the most homework rarely have time to mark it properly, so the effort often disappears without a word of feedback. So I would not remove homework completely; I would reduce it, and I would make sure that every task counts for something.

prompt.es: Completa: «La prueba fue un éxito hasta cierto punto; los alumnos aún necesitaban ayuda.»

feedback.es: To a certain extent (o degree) limita el éxito: funcionó, pero no del todo.

origin.text: The results were encouraging, and the trial was a success to a certain ___; however, most pupils still needed a lot of help.

prompt.es: Reescribe con acuerdo parcial: Tom tiene razón, pero su idea tiene un problema.

answer.text: Tom is right up to a point, but his idea has a drawback.
accepted: Tom is right up to a point, but his idea has a drawback.
I partly agree with Tom, but his idea has a drawback.
Tom is partly right, but his idea has a drawback.
Tom is right to a certain extent, but his idea has a drawback.
I agree with Tom to a certain extent, but his idea has a drawback.
Tom is partly right, but his idea has a problem.

feedback.es: Up to a point o partly convierten un acuerdo total en parcial, y drawback nombra el problema con precisión.

origin.text: Tom is right, but his idea has a problem.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la idea principal del autor?

choices.text: That panels improve when guests prepare their speeches more carefully.
That good panels depend on guests who respond to one another.
That races between panellists make a discussion more exciting to follow.

feedback.es: Contrasta los discursos preparados con el intercambio real: lo que da forma a una mesa es responder a lo que dijo el otro.

origin.text: Some participants treat a panel like a race: each one waits for a gap, then delivers a prepared speech that ignores what came before. The best panels feel different. Someone says I take your point, but, and suddenly the conversation has a shape.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué hace la moderadora al final?

choices.text: She disputes Sara's point and asks Carlos to answer it on her behalf.
She thanks Carlos for the trial and asks the audience for questions.
She acknowledges Sara and asks Carlos a precise question about the trial.

feedback.es: Reconoce el punto de Sara y pasa el turno a Carlos con una pregunta precisa sobre su experiencia.

origin.audio: That was a valid point, Sara, and it leads me to one question. Carlos, you have run the trial for a full term: did pupils read more, or only faster?
